paragraphs.source_en: Selim I did not proclaim himself the caliph. He dispatched the caliph, Al-Mutawakkil, descendant of the members of the Abbasid dynasty who had survived the Mongol sacking of Baghdad and taken refuge with the Mamluks, from Cairo to Istanbul.” Along with the caliph and Christian, Jewish, and Muslim artisans, merchants, and government officials, he also shipped the holy relics of 140 THE OTTOMANS Muhammad there, which the Ottomans encased in gold and precious jewels. These included his mantle, battle standard, sword, bow, beard hair, a tooth, and a footprint, as well as the mantle and prayer mat of his daughter and wife of Ali, Fatima. The holy loot included the swords of Muhammad’s companions, the cooking pot of Abraham, Joseph’s robe, Moses’s staff, and King David's sword for good measure. The Ottomans also kept relics from John the Baptist taken in their conquests.
